title: GitHub Trending Summary - Weekly - 2026-10-21
ranking_basis: GitHub Trending weekly star gains for ranks 1-12; Search freshness candidates appended separately
ranking_explanation: Ranks 1-12 are ordered by the weekly star-gain counters shown on https://github.com/trending?since=weekly at snapshot time, descending. Ranks 13-15 are newly created repos found with GitHub Search, ordered by the rounded current star counts displayed there; their weekly Trending gains are unavailable and they are not directly comparable to ranks 1-12.
global_caveat: GitHub Trending's weekly gain is a point-in-time page counter, not an independently reconstructed historical measure. REA's displayed +157,631 gain is an extreme outlier relative to its total stars and could not be independently reconstructed from historical REST data. Search-only freshness candidates have rounded current star displays, not comparable weekly Trending deltas. Repo descriptions and feature details were checked against first-party READMEs, not independently audited.

themes.title: Agent-native workflows and orchestration
themes.content: Projects connect coding agents to software tools, desktop apps, multi-step workflows, and multi-agent runtimes.

themes.title: Local creative production

themes.title: Science-specific agent tooling
themes.content: Scientific Agent Skills packages reusable research workflows and scientific database access for multiple agent clients.

themes.title: Reverse engineering and security analysis
themes.content: REA adds agent-directed app and binary inspection, while Ghidra represents the established analysis framework in this domain.

themes.title: Model inference infrastructure
themes.content: DeepInfer is a newly created DeepSeek inference release for offline serving, with hardware support and full-stack requirements stated in its README.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-10-21 17:11 UTC. Scope: Weekly. Date range: 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-21. Ranks 1-12 use GitHub Trending weekly gains; ranks 13-15 are fresh Search candidates ordered by rounded current stars, with weekly gains unavailable.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: A sharp outlier leads the weekly Trending page: morluto/rea is shown with 157,631 new stars, far ahead of the rest of the page. The wider snapshot also surfaces newly created repositories in Android TV customization, inference, and agent audio tooling; those search-only candidates have no comparable weekly Trending delta. The common thread remains agents connecting to software and specialized workflows.

sections.title: Top Repositories
sections.content: The first 12 repositories are ranked by the weekly star gains displayed on GitHub Trending. The final three are newly created Search candidates, not comparable by weekly star gain, and are ordered by rounded current stars.

sections.title: morluto/rea
sections.description: An MCP toolkit for agents to inspect web and desktop apps, JavaScript/Electron projects, .NET assemblies, and native binaries, with evidence attached to findings.
sections.why_notable: Its reported weekly gain is an exceptional outlier and it anchors the agent-assisted reverse-engineering theme.
sections.unique_caveat: The weekly gain is extraordinary relative to the repo's total star base; treat it as the reported Trending counter, not an independently reconstructed historical count.

sections.title: debpalash/VoiceStudio
sections.description: A local-first desktop suite for voice cloning and design, dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation.
sections.why_notable: The second-largest gain in this snapshot, reflecting demand for a broad, self-hostable speech-production workflow.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says local workflows are available but remote services are optional, so it is not necessarily an entirely offline-only setup.

sections.title: MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search
sections.description: A job-application workflow that evaluates postings, tailors CVs and cover letters, and prepares interview practice.
sections.why_notable: It turns a general coding agent into a structured end-to-end personal workflow, rather than another general-purpose assistant.
sections.unique_caveat: The project README says the job-portal search skills are Danish-market-focused, although its core evaluation and drafting workflow is designed to generalize.

sections.title: stablyai/orca
sections.description: A desktop and mobile workspace for running coding agents in parallel, isolated Git worktrees.
sections.why_notable: Strong momentum for multi-agent orchestration, with parallel worktrees and remote monitoring as concrete workflow features.

sections.title: NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra
sections.description: A mature software reverse-engineering framework for disassembly, decompilation, scripting, and extensible analysis.
sections.why_notable: It is a notable established-project counterpoint amid the newer agent-first repositories, and complements REA's reverse-engineering signal.

sections.title: heygen-com/hyperframes
sections.description: A framework that turns HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 video.
sections.why_notable: It gives coding agents a production path from authored web content to rendered video, extending the agent workflow beyond code.

sections.title: anomalyco/opencode
sections.description: An open-source AI coding agent with terminal workflows and a desktop app in beta.
sections.why_notable: It remains one of the largest coding-agent projects by total stars while still drawing substantial weekly interest.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository README labels the desktop application beta.

sections.title: anthropics/claude-plugins-official
sections.description: Anthropic's managed directory for Claude Code plugins, including commands, agents, skills, and optional MCP configuration.
sections.why_notable: Its marketplace structure shows the shift from standalone agents toward installable, reusable agent capabilities.
sections.unique_caveat: The README warns that third-party plugin contents are not verified by Anthropic; inspect a plugin before installation.

sections.title: K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills
sections.description: A cross-agent library of scientific skills and connectors to scientific databases.
sections.why_notable: It is the clearest domain-specific example of agent tooling extending into repeatable scientific research workflows.

sections.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
sections.description: A community effort to expose existing desktop and professional software through agent-usable command-line interfaces.
sections.why_notable: It represents the agent-native tooling theme: wrapping established applications in interfaces agents can operate.
sections.unique_caveat: GitHub REST metadata showed its last push on 2026-09-22, older than the seven-day snapshot; its inclusion reflects star momentum, not a recent code update.

sections.title: mksglu/context-mode
sections.description: MCP and hook integrations that sandbox tool output, preserve session context, and route tools across coding-agent platforms.
sections.why_notable: It targets the practical context and tool-output bottlenecks that appear as agents are used for longer coding sessions.

sections.title: ruvnet/ruflo
sections.description: An agent meta-harness for Claude Code and Codex, with core tools, a console, and policy/routing integrations.
sections.why_notable: It adds another multi-agent orchestration approach to a week dominated by systems that compose or extend existing coding agents.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository README identifies one animated download counter as illustrative, not a live download total.

sections.title: Gathin23/cleanyourtv
sections.ranking_status: freshness supplement; not ranked by weekly Trending gain
sections.description: An Android TV cleanup workflow that uses an AI coding assistant and ADB to disable unwanted vendor packages and install a custom launcher.
sections.stars_gained_display: N/A - not available from GitHub Trending
sections.why_notable: GitHub Search places it among the highest-starred repositories created during this seven-day window. Its README describes reversible package disabling rather than uninstalling apps.
sections.unique_caveat: Review device-specific changes before running them; the README describes reversible ADB package-disabling steps and a restore path.

sections.title: deepseek-ai/DeepInfer
sections.ranking_status: freshness supplement; not ranked by weekly Trending gain
sections.description: DeepSeek's open-source offline inference framework for high-throughput production serving.
sections.stars_gained_display: N/A - not available from GitHub Trending
sections.why_notable: It is a newly created, high-star inference project, bringing model-serving infrastructure into the week's fresh-repository signal.
sections.unique_caveat: The README currently lists NVIDIA SM100 and Huawei Ascend 950 support and says a complete serving stack still requires components such as a KV cache.

sections.title: Leonxlnx/earshot
sections.ranking_status: freshness supplement; not ranked by weekly Trending gain
sections.description: Local CPU-based audio analysis and sound-generation tools that let coding agents inspect, critique, and create sound.
sections.stars_gained_display: N/A - not available from GitHub Trending
sections.why_notable: Created during the snapshot window and updated within the past few days, it is a fresh agent-media project with CLI, Python API, and MCP interfaces.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent-native workflows and orchestration: REA, Orca, OpenCode, Claude Plugins, CLI-Anything, Context Mode, Ruflo, and AI Job Search attach agents to concrete tools, apps, and multi-step workflows; CleanYourTV and Earshot extend this to device customization and audio. Local creative production: VoiceStudio emphasizes local speech workflows, while HyperFrames turns authored HTML/CSS and media into rendered video. Science-specific agent tooling: Scientific Agent Skills packages reusable research workflows and scientific database access. Reverse engineering remains a live use case: REA brings agents into app and binary analysis; Ghidra provides the mature analysis framework. Fresh-repository candidates also include DeepInfer for inference. Languages among the 12 Trending-ranked repositories: TypeScript (6), Python (5), and Java (1).

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This week's signal is not just “more coding agents”; it is agents becoming an interface layer for existing software, research, and creative work. REA's reported gain is unusually large and should be read as GitHub Trending's point-in-time counter. Newly created projects in inference, consumer-device customization, and audio show the same agent momentum spilling into more specialized domains, although their weekly star gains are not directly comparable.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary: https://github.com/trending?since=weekly. Corroboration: GitHub REST repository endpoints for Trending metadata; git ls-remote HEAD for current default-branch commits; GitHub Search query pushed:>=2026-10-14 for recent-push signals and created:2026-10-14..2026-10-21 stars:>100 for fresh candidates. The Search page showed rounded star counts for the three freshness additions. Weekly gains are taken from the matching Trending page, not reconstructed from Search API. Ranks 1-12 are descending by reported weekly gains; three newly created Search candidates are appended separately with unavailable weekly gains. REA's displayed gain is an extreme outlier that cannot be independently reconstructed from historical REST data. First-party READMEs were checked for purpose and workflow. No prior-window comparison was available, so no notable-shift claim is included.
